Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child (or children) you're claiming for:**

How old is your child? The age categories are:
- **Under 16** years old
- **16 to 19** years old  
- **20 or over**

Please tell me your child's age, and if you have multiple children you want to claim for, let me know about each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, who is 17 years old and lives with you.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age category), there are additional requirements to check. Let me move to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, for 16-19 year olds like Alex, there are specific requirements. 

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (enrolled and actively studying), OR
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks), OR  
3. **Neither** (not in education/training and didn't recently leave)

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex has left education recently. He's signed up with the local careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying! Since Alex left education recently, let me check the extension eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Alex registering with the local careers service is exactly what's needed. There's a 20-week extension period available for young people aged 16-17 who have left approved education or training and registered with a qualifying service (like a government careers service, Connexions, or armed services).

**To confirm Alex's eligibility for this extension, I need to know:**

1. **When did Alex leave education?** (I need to check if it's been less than 20 weeks)
2. **When did Alex turn 17?** (The extension also ends when the child turns 18, whichever comes first - the 20-week limit or their 18th birthday)

Can you provide these dates?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left education about 3 months ago - so that's around 12 weeks or so. And he turned 17 back in January, so he won't be 18 for quite a while yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's really helpful information. So Alex:
- Left education about 12 weeks ago (well within the 20-week limit)
- Is 17 and won't turn 18 for several months
- Has registered with the local careers service

This means Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension period. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Children aged 16+ who work 24 hours or more per week are not eligible for Child Benefit unless they're also in approved education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now. He's just been focusing on figuring out his next steps with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex isn't working at all, that requirement is met. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about benefits.

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits

If Alex is NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right, that's fine and we can continue.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. Nothing like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships.

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?** If so, what type and in which country (England, Scotland, or Wales)?

The rules vary by region:
- **All apprenticeships in England** disqualify from Child Benefit
- **Modern Apprenticeships in Scotland** disqualify
- **Most Welsh apprenticeships** disqualify, EXCEPT Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales are approved

If Alex is NOT in any apprenticeship at all, that's fine.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. He's just registered with the careers service at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, we can continue. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is about YOU as the claimant.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If yes, that satisfies the residency requirement. There are also several other ways to meet this requirement (such as through EU Settlement Scheme status, or being a Crown servant abroad), but normally living in the UK is the most straightforward.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm here in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives with you at home, so this requirement should be straightforward.

**Do you live with Alex?** (You already mentioned this, but I want to confirm)

If yes, that satisfies the responsibility requirement. There are also other ways to show responsibility, such as contributing to their upkeep or paying maintenance, but living with the child is the most common way.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

If no one else is claiming, that's fine. If someone else is claiming but you've both agreed that you should claim instead, that can also work.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, we can proceed. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation. You mentioned Alex lives at home with you, but I need to confirm a few things:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital** (for an extended period)
2. **In care** (local authority care)
3. **Being fostered**
4. **Living normally at home with you** (none of the above apply)

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is just living normally at home with me. None of those other situations apply.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final check:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child. Since Alex lives at home with you and you're looking after him, I expect the answer is no, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I'm supporting him myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why You're Eligible:

Alex qualifies under the **20-week extension rule** for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education. Specifically:

- ✅ Alex is 17 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- ✅ Alex left education about 12 weeks ago (well within the 20-week limit)
- ✅ Alex has registered with the local careers service (a qualifying service)
- ✅ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (living together)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards Alex's care

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate

### Important Things to Know:

- **20-week extension**: Your eligibility under the extension rule will last until either 20 weeks from when Alex left education OR when Alex turns 18 (whichever comes first). Since Alex left education about 12 weeks ago, you have approximately 8 more weeks under this extension.

- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: Be aware that if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge (a tax charge). However, you can still claim and may want to for National Insurance credit purposes.

- **Payment schedule**: Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Where to Apply:

Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

If you have any questions about your claim, feel free to ask!
